5	/// AD-3 — the one closed `Failure` hierarchy, exactly 14 subtypes: the 13
6	/// codes from `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md` plus the local-only
7	/// `malformedResponse` (client-side parse failure, never sent by the
8	/// backend). Never redefined or subset per feature; every repository method
9	/// returns `Either<Failure, T>` built from this type (RNF09).
10	///
11	/// `retryable` is derived here, once, from the 6 server `retryable:true`
12	/// codes (AD-4) — no other file re-decides which codes retry.
13	@freezed
14	sealed class Failure with _$Failure {
15	  const factory Failure.authExpired({required String message}) = AuthExpired;
16	  const factory Failure.authInvalid({required String message}) = AuthInvalid;
17	  const factory Failure.networkTimeout({required String message}) =
18	      NetworkTimeout;
19	  const factory Failure.networkOffline({required String message}) =
20	      NetworkOffline;
21	  const factory Failure.validation({required String message}) = Validation;
22	  const factory Failure.piiCheckFailed({required String message}) =
23	      PiiCheckFailed;
24	  const factory Failure.embeddingFailed({required String message}) =
25	      EmbeddingFailed;
26	  const factory Failure.aiGenerationTimeout({required String message}) =
27	      AiGenerationTimeout;
28	  const factory Failure.notFound({required String message}) = NotFound;
29	  const factory Failure.rateLimited({required String message}) = RateLimited;
30	  const factory Failure.exportEmptyPeriod({required String message}) =
31	      ExportEmptyPeriod;
32	  const factory Failure.payloadTooLarge({required String message}) =
33	      PayloadTooLarge;
34	  const factory Failure.ocrNoText({required String message}) = OcrNoText;
35	
36	  /// Local-only — the client's own parse-failure detection. `retryable` is
37	  /// hardcoded `false` for this subtype (AD-3).
38	  const factory Failure.malformedResponse({required String message}) =
39	      MalformedResponse;
40	
41	  const Failure._();
42	
43	  /// The 6 server `retryable:true` codes (AD-4). Every other code —
44	  /// including the local `malformedResponse` — is `false`.
45	  bool get retryable => switch (this) {
46	        NetworkTimeout() => true,
47	        NetworkOffline() => true,
48	        PiiCheckFailed() => true,
49	        EmbeddingFailed() => true,
50	        AiGenerationTimeout() => true,
51	        RateLimited() => true,
52	        AuthExpired() ||
53	        AuthInvalid() ||
54	        Validation() ||
55	        NotFound() ||
56	        ExportEmptyPeriod() ||
57	        PayloadTooLarge() ||
58	        OcrNoText() ||
59	        MalformedResponse() =>
60	          false,
61	      };
62	
63	  /// Maps a backend error `code` (`error-taxonomy.md`) to its `Failure`
64	  /// subtype. An unrecognized code (should never happen — the taxonomy is
65	  /// closed) falls back to [Failure.malformedResponse] rather than throwing,
66	  /// so no repository ever lets an unmapped error escape (RNF09).
67	  factory Failure.fromCode(String code, String message) => switch (code) {
68	        'AUTH_EXPIRED' => Failure.authExpired(message: message),
69	        'AUTH_INVALID' => Failure.authInvalid(message: message),
70	        'NETWORK_TIMEOUT' => Failure.networkTimeout(message: message),
71	        'NETWORK_OFFLINE' => Failure.networkOffline(message: message),
72	        'VALIDATION_ERROR' => Failure.validation(message: message),
73	        'PII_CHECK_FAILED' => Failure.piiCheckFailed(message: message),
74	        'EMBEDDING_FAILED' => Failure.embeddingFailed(message: message),
75	        'AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT' =>
76	          Failure.aiGenerationTimeout(message: message),
77	        'NOT_FOUND' => Failure.notFound(message: message),
78	        'RATE_LIMITED' => Failure.rateLimited(message: message),
79	        'EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD' => Failure.exportEmptyPeriod(message: message),
80	        'PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE' => Failure.payloadTooLarge(message: message),
81	        'OCR_NO_TEXT' => Failure.ocrNoText(message: message),
82	        _ => Failure.malformedResponse(message: message),
83	      };
84	}

1	# Cerne — Requirements and Screen Flow
2	
3	Cerne is a reflective-journaling mobile app with an AI assistant. The user records their day by text, audio or photo; a conversational agent consults those records (semantic search) to answer with context and to offer insights.
4	
5	This document is the product specification. The visual reference is the prototype in `docs/input/prototype/`; the backend API is documented in `docs/input/backend/`.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. Functional requirements
10	
11	### RF01 — Multimodal capture (text / audio / photo)
12	Data entry by text, real-time audio recording and photo upload — always through Screen 2 (Insertion Modal), which has a raw text field in addition to the microphone and the gallery. Every capture becomes a persisted record (`POST /entries`), **distinct from a chat message** (see the separation note in RF04).
13	
14	**Acceptance criteria:**
15	- The three modalities (text, audio, photo) result in the same persisted-entry format — none is treated structurally differently from the others after capture.
16	- Cancelling a capture midway (e.g., interrupting a recording) does not create a partial or empty entry.
17	
18	### RF02 — Speech-to-text / OCR processing
19	Transcription of audio (speech-to-text) and recognition of text in images (OCR) over the content captured in RF01.
20	
21	**Acceptance criteria:** four visible states — recording, processing, transcribed, transcription error.
22	
23	### RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
24	Access barrier via Face ID / Touch ID / PIN before exposing the user's data.
25	
26	**Acceptance criteria:**
27	- A biometric failure (e.g., fingerprint not recognized) offers PIN as an alternative, without locking the user out of the app.
28	- The app, sent to the background and resumed after 5 minutes, requires authentication again — it does not stay unlocked indefinitely (fixed value, not configurable by the user).
29	
30	### RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
31	Continuous conversation with the AI agent, with semantic search over previous entries. **Chat messages are conversational and do not create journal entries automatically** — the only exception is the explicit save action described in RF10. Otherwise, the chat queries existing entries via RAG but does not write to them.
32	
33	**Acceptance criteria:**
34	- Three mandatory UI states: processing/streaming, error, complete response.
35	- If the response stream drops midway, the partial message stays visible with a failure indication (it does not disappear).
36	
37	### RF05 — Personal summary export
38	Generation of a narrative summary by AI (Claude Haiku 4.5) from the user's entries, exportable as PDF, with an additional option to download the raw data without the narrative. No clinical or diagnostic connotation. **Scope: job generation, file download and failure handling — never the quality of the generated narrative text.**
39	
40	**Acceptance criteria:**
41	- An export job with zero entries in the period returns a handled error state (not an empty PDF, not a crash).
42	- A failure generating the narrative text (model timeout) still allows downloading the raw data without the narrative — the export is not blocked by an AI failure.
43	
44	### RF06 — Semantic search / filter over journal entries
45	Semantic similarity search (via Voyage AI embeddings, reusing the ones already generated in RF01) combined with metadata filters (date, entry type). There is no filter by tag or category: the backend does not implement it in any endpoint — `GET /entries` and `GET /entries/search` accept only `source` and `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Tags appear only embedded, read-only, in the `Entry` object (see section 2).
46	
47	**Acceptance criteria:**
48	- Searching for a term finds semantically related entries even without the exact word (e.g., searching "ansiedade" returns an entry that only mentions "nervosismo", without the literal term).
49	- 300 ms search debounce: fast typing triggers a single query, not one per keystroke.
50	- Results from the local read cache stay consistent with the server after reconnection, without duplicating displayed items *(the architecture is cloud-only; offline allows only viewing already-cached data, not writing)*.
51	- Two or more filters applied at the same time (`source` + `dateFrom`/`dateTo`) narrow results with AND logic (not OR).
52	- Clearing the filters returns to the full list without restarting the screen.
53	
54	### RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)
55	A screen whose state depends simultaneously on authentication, synchronization status and entry data.
56	
57	**Acceptance criteria:**
58	- Session expiration while viewing triggers a new-login prompt without a crash and without losing the scroll position.
59	- The per-entry synchronization status badge updates independently of the authentication stream.
60	- No BLoC imports another BLoC directly.

This explicitly should apply to the export job's combined `status`/`narrativeStatus` state (not named in AD-12's binds list yet, but the same rule plainly fits — two independent axes can't be squeezed into `Resource<T>`).

## 6. Bottom sheet precedent (`EntriesFilterSheet.show`)

`lib/features/entries/presentation/widgets/entries_filter_sheet.dart:70-114` is the clearest, most recent precedent (explicitly says it "mirrors `InsertionModal.show()`'s own bottom-sheet choreography"):

```dart
static Future<void> show(BuildContext context, {...}) async {
  final reduceMotion = MediaQuery.of(context).disableAnimations;
  final controller = BottomSheet.createAnimationController(Navigator.of(context))
    ..duration = reduceMotion ? Duration.zero : DesignTokens.durationSheetUp
    ..reverseDuration = reduceMotion ? Duration.zero : null;
  try {
    await showModalBottomSheet<void>(
      context: context,
      isScrollControlled: true,
      useSafeArea: true,
      barrierColor: DesignTokens.colorScrimHeavy,
      backgroundColor: Colors.transparent,
      elevation: 0,
      transitionAnimationController: controller,
      builder: (_) => EntriesFilterSheet(...),
    );
  } finally {
    // waits for reverse animation to finish (AnimationStatus.dismissed) before controller.dispose()
  }
}
```
- Sheet's own `build()` (lines 160-169): `Container` with `padding: DesignTokens.screenPadding`, `decoration: BoxDecoration(color: DesignTokens.colorSurfaceElevated, borderRadius: BorderRadius.vertical(top: Radius.circular(DesignTokens.radiusLg)), boxShadow: DesignTokens.elevation2)`, wrapped in `SafeArea(top: false)` + `SingleChildScrollView` (Dynamic-Type overflow guard).
- Reduce Motion: driven by `MediaQuery.of(context).disableAnimations` → zero-duration controller, same pattern must be reused for the export sheet (which per the AC "replaces its content in place" — i.e., state transitions inside the sheet should NOT re-trigger this open/close choreography, only content swap within one still-open sheet instance).
- Design tokens referenced in this precedent that story 7.1's AC explicitly names: `DesignTokens.radiusLg` (`lib/core/design_tokens.dart:207`, value `24`), `DesignTokens.elevation2` (line 226, a `List<BoxShadow>`), `DesignTokens.durationSheetUp` (line 244, `200ms`), `DesignTokens.colorScrimHeavy` (line 85), `DesignTokens.colorSurfaceElevated`.
- `InsertionModal` (`lib/features/capture/presentation/widgets/insertion_modal.dart`) is the other/original precedent `EntriesFilterSheet.show` explicitly mirrors — worth reading directly if a tabbed/multi-step sheet layout is needed (export sheet needs in-place content replacement across 5-6 states, closer to a single evolving `BlocBuilder`-driven body than `InsertionModal`'s tab switcher, but same shell).
